# RNA: WGCNA

## Load packages

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| output: false

rm(list=ls())

pkgs <- c("tidyverse", "dplyr", "readr", "magrittr", "ggplot2","readxl",
          "cowplot", "GGally", "knitr","kableExtra", "data.table", 
          "skimr", "flextable", "Metrics", "ggvenn", "devtools","ape",
         "Biostrings", "DECIPHER", "edgeR", "WGCNA", "Spectra", "rpx",
         "mzR", "RCy3")
for (i in seq_along(pkgs)){
  pkg <- pkgs[[i]]
  tryCatch(if(pkg%in%rownames(installed.packages())){
    cat("Available:", pkg, "\n")
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
    cat("Package loaded:", pkg,"\n")
  }
  else if(!(pkg%in%rownames(installed.packages()))){
    install.packages("BiocManager")
    BiocManager::install(pkg)
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
    cat("Package loaded:", pkg,"\n")
  }
 else{
    cat("Not available:",pkg,">> now installing...", "\n")
    install.packages(pkg, repos =  "https://cloud.r-project.org")
    cat("Now available:", pkg, "\n")
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
    cat("Package loaded:", pkg,"\n")
  }
  )
}

```

## Read data

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

##########################################################################
## Gene expression
##
## Read the gene expression and only select columns containing individual 
## information and gene expression levels and remove NA
#########################################################################

f_mice_gexp <- read_csv(ff1, col_select = c(1,9:143), show_col_types = F)|>
  drop_na()
f_mice_gexp[1:5, 1:5] ## View some of the data

##########################################################################
## Phenotype
##
## Read the trait and only select columns containing Mice IDs and variables
## of interest, select the female using filter(), and remove NA
#########################################################################

f_mice_y <- read_csv(ff2, col_select = c("Mice", "sex", "weight_g",
                                         "100xfat_weight","total_fat",
                                         "Total_Chol", "HDL_Chol"), 
                         show_col_types = F)|>
  filter(sex==2)|>
  drop_na()
f_mice_y[1:5, 1:5] ## View some of the data

# Match the IDs (column names) in the gene expression data with the 
# IDs (first column) in the trait

common <- intersect(colnames(f_mice_gexp)[-1], f_mice_y$Mice)

## Select only IDs in both gene expression and trait

f_mice1 <- f_mice_gexp|>
  select(common)

f_mice_trait <- f_mice_y[f_mice_y$Mice%in%common,-2] #drop the sex in column 2

```

## Quality Control

```{r}
## Transpose the gene expression to ensure samples are in rows and 
## genes are in columns. Then convert it to a data frame and 
## rename the columns using gene IDs in the original f_mice_gexp object

f_mice <- as.data.frame(t(f_mice1), header=T) 
names(f_mice) <- f_mice_gexp$substanceBXH

## Check for outliers in your gene
gsg.F <- goodSamplesGenes(f_mice)
summary(gsg.F)
gsg.F$allOK # A true value indicates no outlier
```


```{r}
#| fig-show: hide

## Clustering samples based on average distance between clusters before merging
sampleTree.F <- hclust(dist(f_mice), method = "average") 

#Plotting the cluster dendrogram
plot(sampleTree.F, 
     main = "Sample clustering to detect outliers \n Female", sub="",
     xlab="", cex.lab = 1, cex.axis = 1, cex.main = 1)
```

## Network Construction

```{r}
#| warning: false

#########################################################################
## Calculate Soft power threshold for the network
##
## The 'pickSoftThreshold' helps in selecting the power needed to set the 
## threshold for the similarity between expression levels of genes before
## computing the network adjacency matrix
##
## In the first plot, we set the R^2 to 0.80 and any power (from 1-15) that
## exceeds that and also have the highest mean connectivity (in the second plot)
## will be chosen as the power
########################################################################

spt.F <- pickSoftThreshold(f_mice)

plot(spt.F$fitIndices[,1], spt.F$fitIndices[,2], type="n", ####
     main = "Female: Scale Independence",
     xlab = "Soft Threshold (power)", 
     ylab = "Scale-free Topology,signed R.sq")
text(spt.F$fitIndices[,1], spt.F$fitIndices[,2], col="purple")
abline(h=0.80, col="purple")

plot(spt.F$fitIndices[,1], spt.F$fitIndices[,5], type="n", 
     main = "Female: Mean connectivity",
     xlab = "Soft Threshold (power)", ylab = "Mean connectivity")
text(spt.F$fitIndices[,1], spt.F$fitIndices[,5], col="purple")


## Calling adjacency
## Although I gave you 6, 7 actually exceeds the 0.80 R^2 and highest mean among
## power that exceeds 0.80
sp.F <- 7

adj.F <- adjacency(f_mice, power = sp.F)
```

## Module Construction

```{r}

## Defining dissimilarity in the adjacency matrix

TOM.F <- TOMsimilarity(adj.F) ## First obtain the similarity
TOM.dissim.F <- 1-TOM.F ## Then 1-similarity give dissimilarity

## Hierarchical clustering analysis to visualize the dissimilairty clusters

geneT.F <- hclust(as.dist(TOM.dissim.F), method = "average")

## Set module size for the gene dendogram and the minimum gene cluster size

mod.F <- cutreeDynamic(dendro=geneT.F, distM = TOM.dissim.F, deepSplit = 2,
                       pamRespectsDendro = FALSE, minClusterSize = 30)


## Module color
## Assign color to each gene module

mod.col.F <- labels2colors(mod.F)

## Plot the gene dendogram with module color
plotDendroAndColors(geneT.F, mod.col.F, "Module", dendroLabels=FALSE, hang=0.03,
                    addGuide=TRUE, guideHang=0.05,
                    main="Female: Gene dendogram and module colors")


## Module Eigengene Identification

MElist.F <- moduleEigengenes(f_mice, colors=mod.col.F)

MEs.F <- MElist.F$eigengenes #Retrieve the eigengene list
```

## Module merging

```{r}
##############################################################################
## To synthesize module detection and for computational efficiency, we want to
## merge modules with highly correlated eigengenes
#############################################################################

## Eigengene dissimilarity

ME.dissim.F <- 1-cor(MElist.F$eigengenes, use="complete")

## Clustering eigengenes dissimilarity
## Here the clustering reveals gene modules that can be merged together based on
## their dissimilarity

METree.F <- hclust(as.dist(ME.dissim.F), method="average")

## plot tree showing clustering of eigengenes with a cut-off of 0.25
plot(as.dendrogram(METree.F), main = "Female: Cluster of module eigengenes")
abline(h=.25, col="red")

## Merge module
## Here gene modules in a hierarchical cluster below the 0.25 height will be merged
## together

#Threshold for merging modules set at .25
merge.F <- mergeCloseModules(f_mice, mod.col.F, cutHeight=.25) 
merged.col.F=merge.F$colors #merge colors and assign color to each module
mergedMEc.F <- merge.F$newMEs #eigengenes of the new merged modules

## Plot the gene dendogram with module color
plotDendroAndColors(geneT.F, cbind(mod.col.F,merged.col.F), 
                    c("Original Module","Merged Module"), 
                    dendroLabels=FALSE, hang=0.03, addGuide=TRUE, 
                    guideHang=0.05,
                    main="Female: Gene dendogram & module colors for original &
                    merged modules")

```

## Trait matching

### Module-trait association

```{r}
#| fig-show: hide

nGenes_f <- ncol(f_mice) ## obtain the number of genes

nSamples_f <- nrow(f_mice) ## obtain the number of samples

y_f2 <- f_mice_trait|>
  column_to_rownames(var="Mice") ## Change sample IDs from column to rownames

##subset merged eigengenes using the IDs in the trait. Note the IDs are 
## the rownames
mergedMEc.F2 <- mergedMEc.F[rownames(y_f2),] 

## Obtain the correlation and the correlation p-values between the merged 
## eigengenes and the trait

mod.trait.cor_f <- cor(mergedMEc.F2, y_f2, use="p")

mod.trait.pv_f <- corPvalueStudent(mod.trait.cor_f, nSamples_f)

## Plot the Module-trait heatmap
## Specify the how you want the correlation coefficient values and p-values to
## be displayed

textMatrix_f <- paste(signif(mod.trait.cor_f, 2), 
                      "\n(",signif(mod.trait.pv_f,1),")", sep ="");
dim(textMatrix_f) = dim(mod.trait.cor_f)

labeledHeatmap(Matrix = mod.trait.cor_f,
               xLabels = names(y_f2),
               yLabels = names(mergedMEc.F2),
               ySymbols = names(mergedMEc.F2),
               colorLabels = F,
               colors = blueWhiteRed(50),
               textMatrix = textMatrix_f,
               setStdMargins = F,
               cex.text = 0.3,
               zlim = c(-1,1),
               main=paste("Female: Module-trait relationships"),
               cex.lab = 0.4 
               )
```

## Visualize the top 4 module in each trait using a Venn diagram

```{r}
#| warning: false

## Here, the top 4 modules with the highest correlation values and pvalues in 
## each trait are selected to see the number of genes within each module 
##
## You can see that green, magenta, and midnightblue modules have high
## correlation with the selected traits

weight <- list(MLCyan=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="lightcyan"]),
               MGYellow=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="greenyellow"]),
               MCyan=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="cyan"]),
               MMNBlue=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="midnightblue"]))

T_fat <- list(MLCyan=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="lightcyan"]),
              MGYellow=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="greenyellow"]),
              MCyan=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="cyan"]),
              MMNBlue=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="midnightblue"]))

x_fat_wght <- list(MLCyan=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="lightcyan"]),
              MGYellow=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="greenyellow"]),
              MCyan=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="cyan"]),
              MMNBlue=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="midnightblue"]))

T_chol <- list(MLCyan=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="lightcyan"]),
              MGYellow=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="greenyellow"]),
              MGreen=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="green"]),
              MMNBlue=names(f_mice[merged.col.F=="midnightblue"]))
F1 <- ggvenn(weight,
       stroke_size = 0.5, set_name_size = 4, text_size = 3.3, show_percentage = FALSE)

F2 <- ggvenn(T_fat,
       stroke_size = 0.5, set_name_size = 4, text_size = 3.3, show_percentage = FALSE)

F3 <- ggvenn(x_fat_wght,
       stroke_size = 0.5, set_name_size = 4, text_size = 3.3, show_percentage = FALSE)

F4 <- ggvenn(T_chol,
       stroke_size = 0.5, set_name_size = 4, text_size = 3.3, show_percentage = FALSE)

plot_grid(F1,F2,F3,F4, scale = 1, labels = c("A","B", "C", "D"))
```

# MS-Proteomics Data Analysis

```{r}
################################################################################
## Here we are using the 'rpx' package to retrieve data from the ProteomicsXchange
## dataset using the PX project identifier "PXD057454"
## Go here to find more: https://proteomecentral.proteomexchange.org/
## I ensure the dataset has .mzML extension before selecting it. 
## The .mzML extension is one of the mass spectrometry data file extension that
## the Spectra packages accepts
################################################################################

pxd <- PXDataset("PXD057454") #Retrieve the data

## Check the files in the data. Note it prints the first 10 files. To see more, 
## e.g 20, use pxfiles(pxd, n=20).

pxfiles(pxd) 
fl <- "Seq84734_88min_480Ex1.mzML" #select the .mzML file
mz11 <- pxget(pxd,fl) #Download the .mzML file

## Access the raw data and obtain the spectra information, mass-charge values,
## peaks and peak intensity, etc

spt <- Spectra(mz11)

## Plot intensity against mass-charge values

plot(mz(spt)[[1]], intensity(spt)[[1]], type="h", xlab="m/z values",
     ylab="intensity") 

table(msLevel(spt)) #No of MS levels and No of spectra per MS levels

range(rtime(spt)) #Range of retention time

spt1 <- filterMsLevel(spt,1) #Filter MS level 1

spt2 <- filterMsLevel(spt,2) #Filter MS level 2

## Plot total ion current against retention time in MS level 1
plot(rtime(spt1), tic(spt1), type="l", xlab="rtime", ylab="tic", main="MS Level 1")

## Plot total ion current against retention time in MS level 2
plot(rtime(spt2), tic(spt2), type="l", xlab="rtime", ylab="tic", main="MS Level 2")

## Plot intensity against mass-charge values for the first 2000 spectra
plotSpectra(spt[2000])

## Highest precursor intensity for MS level 1
mxm_1 <- max(precursorIntensity(spt1)) 
mxm_1

## Location of highest precursor intensity
wch_1 <- which(precursorIntensity(spt1)==mxm_1) 
wch_1

## Index of the MS level 1 spectrum with the highest precursor intensity
scanIndex(spt1)[wch_1] 

## Highest base peak intensity
mxm_1b <- max(spt1$basePeakIntensity) 
mxm_1b

## Location of highest base peak intensity
which(spt1$basePeakIntensity==mxm_1b)


## Highest precursor intensity for MS level 2
mxm_2 <- max(precursorIntensity(spt2)) 
mxm_2

## Location of highest precursor intensity
wch_2 <- which(precursorIntensity(spt2)==mxm_2) 
wch_2

## Index of the MS2 spectrum with the highest precursor intensity
scanIndex(spt2)[wch_2] 

## Highest base peak intensity
mxm_2b <- max(spt2$basePeakIntensity) 
mxm_2b

## Location of highest base peak intensity
which(spt2$basePeakIntensity==mxm_2b)
```
